angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G: brake into, speed through and drive out of the first real cut), graded by the same code on the matched NFL route families (slant, out, hitch, in, corner) and tested against full-season separation over expected on held-out draft classes, with straight-line speed as the benchmark that does carry; last season's SOE tested against pick order on day 3; 2026 GO/HOLD film queue with coverage and alignment splits.
metric_name: Break G: on the first real cut of a route (30+ degrees after 1.5 yd, entered above 2.5 yd/s), how hard the receiver pushes into the ground over the one second around the break, in g (share of body weight); z within drill and Combine year, averaged over route drills and shrunk for few reps; 1 sd = 0.021 g.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.8, +1.0], n=116 receivers from held-out draft classes; hierarchical model -0.5 [-2.8, +1.8] (167 player-seasons). Same 92 receivers: official 40 vs NFL top speed rho 0.48 [0.35, 0.60]; Combine vs NFL Break G -0.04 [-0.22, 0.14]. Day 3 (20 pairs, 16 receivers, leave-one-class-out): SOE list 3 of 10 vs pick order 4 of 10, difference -10 pts [-36, +12]; gap<32 override wrong 36 per 100 [0, 75], does not beat pick order.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_19/revised applying all round-19 top_changes. Code: the 5,100-line script is replaced by core.py (builders), analysis.py (body numbers, figures, render), appendix.py (TOST, sensitivity) and an independent verify.py that reproduces 30 of 30 checked numbers to the last digit (season/career SOE, baseline R2, delta R2 and interval, held-out slope and interval, TOST arms, speed rho and interval, day-3 half-list test and interval, override error rate, interval and break-even, both sensitivity ranges) using per-statistic seeds. One speed number (0.48, n=92) used in Table 1, Fig 1 and verify.py (the 0.43/0.46 mismatch is gone). Day 3 settled: leave-one-draft-class-out forecasts on every eligible day-3 receiver, receiver-clustered bootstrap and receiver-level permutation (p 0.81): the SOE list does not beat pick order (3/10 vs 4/10); the pick-gap override is reported as an error rate with an interval (36 per 100 [0, 75]) and stated not to beat pick order; Table 2 of round 19 removed. 2026 table: one interval column, man/zone and slot/wide splits with cell n, 'what flips it' column, nine names (three more: Jaylin Lane, Mitch Tinsley, Kayshon Boutte) after dropping the model-probability filter. Writeup: bold plain-words lede, coach-repeatable Break G sentence, SOE defined at first use, result-carrying headings, one reliability/transfer table (6 rows), pooled-speed paragraph and game-speed rerun removed, TOST and sensitivity in the appendix, decisive bottom line (draft order stands on day 3; film queue named), 1,696 words by check.py (round 19: 1,756). Viz: Fig 1 = two panels in one row with n in title and caption; Fig 2 = two-row small multiples (three hardest vs three softest drill cutters) with shared axes and a league-median ghost, text >= 10 pt; Fig 3 = forest of held-out slopes; Fig 4 = compact last-vs-next SOE scatter with list membership plus a pick-gap threshold curve with a receiver-clustered band; Fig 5 uses the same GO (blue circle) / HOLD (orange square) encoding as the table.
open_risks: Still a null-result paper: the actionable output is a film queue, not a validated rule; judges may see the day-3 section as only negative.

Leave-one-draft-class-out forecasts of next-season SOE are poor (held-out rank correlations below zero because the 2024 class alone trains the 2023 fold); the half-list back-test rests on 20 pairs from 16 receivers.
The override error-rate interval [0, 75] is very wide (11 overrides among 11 receivers); the receiver-clustered bootstrap is coarse at this size.
Splits and Fig 2 rest on sampled NFL plays (up to 40 per player, half top-EPA); only 5 of 36 split cells reach 30 snaps.
One outcome-side sensitivity variant puts the held-out slope at -3.0 in per sd, on the harm margin; harm is not excluded.
